newsitem.title: USA: Illinois incinerator bondholders mulling next move.
newsitem.headline: Illinois incinerator bondholders mulling next move.

text.p: Attorneys for holders of bonds sold to finance a waste-to-energy incinerator in Illinois are still plotting their next move more than three weeks after a Cook County, Ill., Circuit Court judge dismissed them from a lawsuit against Illinois officials.
Vince Aquilino, an attorney at Baker & McKenzie who is representing bondholders, said Wednesday that "all litigation strategies available to us" were being evaluated.
On Sept 30, Judge Edwin Berman dismissed bondholders from a lawsuit challenging Illinois' elimination of a subsidy for incinerators.
Berman ruled that bondholders had no standing to bring the lawsuit, which was filed as part of a lawsuit originally brought by the developers of two bond-financed incinerators.

On Wednesday, attorneys for the developers, CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton, were back before Berman for a status on their amended complaint. Jeff Hall, an attorney at Bartlit Beck Herman Palenchar & Scott, who is representing the developers, said oral arguments should be held by Berman sometime before yearend.
At the same time Berman dismissed bondholders from the lawsuit, he also dismissed part of the lawsuit filed by the developers against Illinois Commerce Commission officials earlier this year.

Hall said the amended complaint contained more details about a charge, not dismissed from the lawsuit by the judge, concerning the legality of the state's repeal of a subsidy for the incinerators. Berman had ordered the developers to supply more detailed information about that allegation.

Illinois Development Finance Authority sold $79.5 million of unrated, tax-exempt bonds for an incinerator in Ford Heights in 1994 and the town of Fulton sold $84.6 million of bonds for an incinerator project last December.

While awaiting the outcome of its lawsuit, CGE Ford Heights filed for bankruptcy earlier this year. In May, a federal bankruptcy court judge in Wilmington, Del., approved an agreement between the developer and bondholders to only make interest payments on the bonds until Oct 1, 1997.
